skill.name: Select Executor Type for Parallel Workload
skill.description: Canonical skill for choosing between ThreadPoolExecutor (I/O-bound tasks) and ProcessPoolExecutor (CPU-bound tasks) based on workload characteristics. Both implement the same Executor interface but differ in concurrency model, resource overhead, and GIL interaction.
skill.skill_body:
When designing a parallel application, evaluate your workload characteristics: I/O-bound tasks (network requests, file operations, database queries) are better suited to ThreadPoolExecutor due to lower overhead and shared memory; CPU-bound tasks (computation, data processing) benefit from ProcessPoolExecutor to leverage multiple cores and bypass Python's Global Interpreter Lock. Both expose the same Executor interface (submit, map, shutdown), so the choice is primarily about workload type and resource constraints.

## Objective

Understand when to use threads vs processes for parallel execution
## Applicable Signals

- Designing a new parallel application
- Evaluating concurrency strategy for a workload
- Choosing between thread-based and process-based execution models

## Contraindications

- Already committed to a specific executor type
- Seeking detailed performance benchmarking or profiling results
- Needing real-time performance metrics for a specific system

## Workflow Steps

- Classify the workload: identify whether tasks are primarily I/O-bound or CPU-bound
- For I/O-bound tasks: select ThreadPoolExecutor
- For CPU-bound tasks: select ProcessPoolExecutor
- Document the decision and workload justification

## Constraints

- This is conceptual guidance only; actual performance depends on system configuration, workload specifics, and Python implementation.
- ThreadPoolExecutor is limited by the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) for CPU-bound work.
- ProcessPoolExecutor incurs inter-process communication overhead.

## Cautions

- Do not assume ThreadPoolExecutor is always faster for I/O; measure with your specific workload.
- ProcessPoolExecutor requires picklable callables and may not work with all object types.
- Resource limits (file descriptors, memory) may constrain the number of workers in either executor.

## Output Contract

- A clear decision on which Executor subclass (ThreadPoolExecutor or ProcessPoolExecutor) to instantiate, justified by workload characteristics (I/O-bound vs CPU-bound).
